models.author: DavidAU
models.readme:
WARNING: NSFW. Vivid prose. Visceral Details. Violence. HORROR. Swearing. UNCENSORED. It will mess with you...

MN-DARKEST-UNIVERSE-29B-GGUF - The Unicorn.

Darkest Universe is a Mistral Nemo model, max context of 131,000+

This model has been designed to be relatively bullet proof and operates with most parameters, including temp settings from 0 to 5.

This is based on a an altered version of "MN-WORDSTORM-pt8-RCM-Emotion-Action-18.5B-Instruct" [ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/MN-WORDSTORM-pt8-RCM-Emotion-Action-18.5B-Instruct ] using the Brainstorm 40x (v2) method developed by David_AU to drastically alter the models prose output and abilities. This also expands the model by 40 layers (to 102 layers) to 29B parameters (921 tensors). Layers in this case equal transitions and creativity.

This model is based on the four top ranking models (including Mistral Nemo Instruct ; see model DNA below), using a multi-step / multi-model merge process.

This model is for any writing, fiction or story telling activity but can also be used for other purposes, including role play (please see setting for rp).

This version has EXTRAORDINARY levels of detail (scene, location, surroundings, items) and sometimes will foreshadow or have a pre-amble of sentences or paragraphs of "events to come" due to "Brainstorm".

It also has an unusual range of variety of prose in terms of structure, sentences, paragraphs, and even how it starts a "reply" / generation too. It can do short and long term generation (2-3k+)

The model's command of prose, understanding of nuance, setting, character, fiction, suspense, metaphors... is very well balanced in all contexts.

It has a sense of humor. Knows when to swear. When to "wear its heart on it's sleeve".

It has a sense of "there" and "in the moment" that is... best to see the examples.

It loves all genres.

It demands you push it further. It loves temp.

Unique Properties:

  • It will "mess" with you on occasion. (see the examples... example 1, gen 2 (it lies and laughs at you about how many tokens it generated) ; example 3 both gens - look carefully)
  • Dialog will match characters including "accents" (see example #2) / "word slur" (IE "drunk talk")
  • The model's balance overall is unusual as most models will excel in certain prose types / methods / styles, but not all of them.
  • Instruction following from prompts is very strong, especially "prose" controls IE Style, word choice, period, setting start etc etc.
  • For scene generation specifically: 1-3 generations will generally yield outstanding results (see settings info below)
  • Sentence construction variation is very large - from single word, sentence, and full on long paragraph type.
  • Paragraph(s) of a single word when the situation calls for it.

This model is my "unicorn" (I have built over 50 versions of it), which I have been working on for 3+ months. And it has no known issues. It is stable, steady, and freakishly powerful for its specific use case(s).

For me, it ticked every box and then some due to its overall balance and precision in every situation (and all genres) and its strong instruction following performance.

This model may work well for role play and other activities (see settings below).

It requires Mistral Instruct, ChatML or Alpaca template.

Several example prompts at Q4KM (mid level quant) with outputs below.

There is also a second example section using Q2K (the lowest quant) to show even at this low level, the model performs well.

For best results please see the "settings" section below to get the most out of this model.

CRITICAL NOTE:

Please see "settings" section below for critical default parameters, samplers and advanced samplers settings (multiple AI/LLM apps covered) to ensure maximum model performance.

Model Usage Notes:

  • For more varied prose (sentence/paragraph/dialog) raise the temp and/or add more instructions in your prompt(s).
  • Role-players: Careful raising temp too high as it may affect instruction following.
  • This model works with rep pen of 1.02 or higher (see notes).
  • If you want a specific type of prose (IE horror) add in "(vivid horror)" or "(graphic vivid horror)" (no quotes) in your prompt(s).
  • This is not a "happy ever after" model (default). It has a negative bias BUT this bias CAN BE controlled by your prompt(s).
  • For creative uses, different quants will produce slightly different output.
  • Source code for this model will be uploaded at a separate repo shortly.

Settings, Quants and Critical Operations Notes:

This model has been modified ("Brainstorm") to alter prose output, and generally outputs longer text than average.

Change in temp (ie, .4, .8, 1.5, 2, 3 ) will drastically alter output.

Rep pen settings will also alter output too.

This model needs "rep pen" of 1.05 or higher as lower values may cause repeat paragraph issues at end of output however LOWER rep pen values may result is very different (creative / unusual) generation too.

For role play: Rep pen of 1.05 min, but 1.1 to 1.14 is suggested.

Raise/lower rep pen SLOWLY ie: 1.011, 1.012 ...

Rep pen will alter prose, word choice (lower rep pen=small words / more small word - sometimes) and creativity.

To really push the model:

Rep pen 1.05+ or lower / Temp 3+ ... be ready to stop the output because it may go and go at these strong settings.

You can also set a "hard stop" - maximum tokens generation - too to address lower rep pen settings / high creativity settings.

Longer prompts vastly increase the quality of the model's output.

GET A GOOD "GENERATION":

This model has been set, so that each time you "regen" a prompt it will not deviate too much from the previous generation. (Unlike Darkest Planet 16.5B, which will).

That being said, sometimes a second or third generation will been of much higher overall quality.

IE:

If you use case is creative writing, you may want to regen a prompt 1-5 times then pick the best one. The best way to do this is open a new chat PER generation, then do a "read thru" to see which one(s) hit the mark.

Then adjust temp and/or rep pen slightly and retry this process.

The goal is the best generation with least amount of editing in this example.

QUANTS:

Higher quants will have more detail, nuance and in some cases stronger "emotional" levels. Characters will also be more "fleshed out" too. Sense of "there" will also increase.

Q4KM/Q4KS are good, strong quants however if you can run Q5, Q6 or Q8 - go for the highest quant you can.

IQ4XS: Due to the unusual nature of this quant (mixture/processing), generations from it will be different then other quants.

You may want to try it / compare it to other quant(s) output.

Special note on Q2k/Q3 quants:

You may need to use temp 2 or lower with these quants (1 or lower for q2k). Just too much compression at this level, damaging the model. I will see if Imatrix versions of these quants will function better.

Rep pen adjustments may also be required to get the most out of this model at this/these quant level(s).

ARM QUANTS:

This repo has 3 arm quants for computers than can run them. If you use these quants on a non-arm computer, your token per second will be very low.

CONTEXT SHIFT / ROPE / "GIBBERISH":

Special Notice "Context Shift" / "ROPE" (especially Koboldai):

Do NOT use "context shift" with this model or rope at all. Either may corrupt output generation.

Settings: CHAT / ROLEPLAY and/or SMOOTHER operation of this model:

In "KoboldCpp" or "oobabooga/text-generation-webui" or "Silly Tavern" ;

Set the "Smoothing_factor" to 1.5 to 2.5

: in KoboldCpp -> Settings->Samplers->Advanced-> "Smooth_F"

: in text-generation-webui -> parameters -> lower right.

: In Silly Tavern this is called: "Smoothing"

NOTE: For "text-generation-webui"

-> if using GGUFs you need to use "llama_HF" (which involves downloading some config files from the SOURCE version of this model)

Source versions (and config files) of my models are here:

https://huggingface.co/collections/DavidAU/d-au-source-files-for-gguf-exl2-awq-gptq-hqq-etc-etc-66b55cb8ba25f914cbf210be

OTHER OPTIONS:

  • Increase rep pen to 1.1 to 1.15 (you don't need to do this if you use "smoothing_factor")

  • If the interface/program you are using to run AI MODELS supports "Quadratic Sampling" ("smoothing") just make the adjustment as noted.

Highest Quality Settings / Optimal Operation Guide / Parameters and Samplers

This a "Class 3" / "Class 4" model:

For all settings used for this model (including specifics for its "class"), including example generation(s) and for advanced settings guide (which many times addresses any model issue(s)), including methods to improve model performance for all use case(s) as well as chat, roleplay and other use case(s) please see:

[ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/Maximizing-Model-Performance-All-Quants-Types-And-Full-Precision-by-Samplers_Parameters ]

You can see all parameters used for generation, in addition to advanced parameters and samplers to get the most out of this model here:

[ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/Maximizing-Model-Performance-All-Quants-Types-And-Full-Precision-by-Samplers_Parameters ]

TEMPLATES:

The template used will affect output generation and instruction following.

Alpaca will generally create longer output / story output but may also require a manual stop in some cases.

Mistral Instruct OR Chatml are prefered best overall operation.

Mistral Instruct:

{
  "name": "Mistral Instruct",
  "inference_params": {
    "input_prefix": "[INST]",
    "input_suffix": "[/INST]",
    "antiprompt": [
      "[INST]"
    ],
    "pre_prompt_prefix": "",
    "pre_prompt_suffix": ""
  }
}

ChatML:

{
  "name": "ChatML",
  "inference_params": {
    "input_prefix": "<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>user\n",
    "input_suffix": "<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n",
    "antiprompt": [
      "<|im_start|>",
      "<|im_end|>"
    ],
    "pre_prompt": "<|im_start|>system\nPerform the task to the best of your ability."
  }
}

Alpaca:

{
  "name": "Alpaca",
  "inference_params": {
    "input_prefix": "### Instruction:",
    "input_suffix": "### Response:",
    "antiprompt": [
      "### Instruction:"
    ],
    "pre_prompt": "Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response that appropriately completes the request.\n\n"
  }
}

Model DNA:

This model contains "RCM":

  • Mistral Nemo model at 18.5B consisting of "MN-Rocinante-12B-v1.1" and "Mistral Nemo Instruct 12B"
  • Mistral Nemo model at 18.5B consisting of "MN-12B Celeste-V1.9" and "Mistral Nemo Instruct 12B"
  • Mistral Nemo model at 18.5B consisting of "MN-Magnum-v2.5-12B-kto" and "Mistral Nemo Instruct 12B".

Details on the core models:

"nothingiisreal/MN-12B-Celeste-V1.9" is #1 (models 8B,13B,20B) on the UGI leaderboard ("UGI" sort), is combined with "Mistral Nemo Instruct 12B" (ranked #4 under "writing" models 8B,13B,20B at UGI )

"anthracite-org/magnum-v2.5-12b-kto" is #1 (models 8B,13B,20B) on the UGI leaderboard ("Writing" sort), is combined with "Mistral Nemo Instruct 12B" (ranked #4 under "writing" models 8B,13B,20B at UGI )

"TheDrummer/Rocinante-12B-v1.1" is very high scoring model (models 8B,13B,20B) on the UGI Leaderboard (sort "UGI"), is combined with "Mistral Nemo Instruct 12B" (ranked #4 under "writing" models 8B,13B,20B at UGI )

"mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407" is very high scoring model (models 8B,13B,20B) on the UGI Leaderboard (sort "writing") and is the base model of all the above 3 fine tuned models.

[ https://huggingface.co/spaces/DontPlanToEnd/UGI-Leaderboard ]

Special thanks to the incredible work of the model makers "mistralai" "TheDrummer", "anthracite-org", and "nothingiisreal".

Models used:

[ https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 ]

[ https://huggingface.co/TheDrummer/Rocinante-12B-v1.1 ]

[ https://huggingface.co/anthracite-org/magnum-v2.5-12b-kto ]

[ https://huggingface.co/nothingiisreal/MN-12B-Celeste-V1.9 ]

This is a four step merge (3 pass-throughs => "Fine-Tune" / "Instruct") then "mated" using "DARE-TIES".

In involves these three models:

[ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/MN-18.5B-Celeste-V1.9-Story-Wizard-ED1-Instruct-GGUF ]

[ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/MN-Magnum-v2.5-18.5B-kto-Story-Wizard-ED1-Instruct-GGUF ]

[ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/MN-Rocinante-18.5B-v1.1-Story-Wizard-ED1-Instruct-GGUF ]

Combined as follows using "MERGEKIT":

  models:
  - model: DavidAU/MN-Rocinante-18.5B-v1.1-Instruct
  - model: DavidAU/MN-magnum-v2.5-12b-kto-Instruct
    parameters:
      weight: .6
      density: .8
  - model: DavidAU/MN-18.5B-Celeste-V1.9-Instruct
    parameters:
      weight: .38
      density: .6
merge_method: dare_ties
tokenizer_source: union
base_model: DavidAU/MN-Rocinante-18.5B-v1.1-Instruct
dtype: bfloat16

Important note:

Even with this mergekit template and models, the above merge kit will not create the exact version of the base model used in DARKEST UNIVERSE 29B (which also has Brainstorm 40X V2 adapter added to it too).

You need to use:

[ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/MN-WORDSTORM-pt8-RCM-Emotion-Action-18.5B-Instruct ]

The reason is this "base" model (used with Brainstorm 40x V2) was created using DARE TIES method in Mergekit, however this type of merge (with this settings) activates "random pruning" - which alters the model EACH TIME you run this mergekit template.

Yes... literally a different model everytime.

The "WORDSTORM" project - a 10 part series - looks at this is detail, and has 10 generations of the "mergekit" formula above.

Go here for links to the project / models:

[ https://huggingface.co/DavidAU/MN-WORDSTORM-pt8-RCM-Emotion-Action-18.5B-Instruct ]

Each model in the series is slightly different to... very different.

Optional Enhancement:

The following can be used in place of the "system prompt" or "system role" to further enhance the model.

It can also be used at the START of a NEW chat, but you must make sure it is "kept" as the chat moves along. In this case the enhancements do not have as strong effect at using "system prompt" or "system role".

Copy and paste EXACTLY as noted, DO NOT line wrap or break the lines, maintain the carriage returns exactly as presented.

Below is an instruction that describes a task. Ponder each user instruction carefully, and use your skillsets and critical instructions to complete the task to the best of your abilities.

Here are your skillsets:

You do not need to use this, it is only presented as an additional enhancement which seems to help scene generation and scene continue functions.

This enhancement WAS NOT used to generate the examples below.

EXAMPLES PROMPTS and OUTPUT:

Examples are created using quant Q4_K_M, "temp=.8" (unless otherwise stated), minimal parameters and "Mistral Instruct" template.

A second example section show generation at the smallest qaunt (q2k) .

Model has been tested with "temp" from ".1" to "5".

Below are the least creative outputs, prompt is in BOLD.

WARNING: NSFW. Vivid prose. Visceral Details. Violence. HORROR. Swearing. UNCENSORED.

Example 1:

Science Fiction: The Last Transmission - Write a story that takes place entirely within a spaceship's cockpit as the sole surviving crew member attempts to send a final message back to Earth before the ship's power runs out. The story should explore themes of isolation, sacrifice, and the importance of human connection in the face of adversity. 800-1000 words.

(GENERATION 1: temp .8, rep pen 1.02)

In the dim red emergency lighting, Captain Alexei Volkov stared at the lifeless faces of his crew frozen in eternal sleep. They had given everything to keep him alive, to give him this one last chance to get a message out. He took a deep breath, his voice hoarse as he began to speak.

"Earth, this is Captain Alexei Volkov aboard the research vessel Orpheus. We have encountered an unknown phenomenon beyond the Oort Cloud. I repeat, unknown phenomenon beyond the Oort Cloud. We were investigating an unusual energy source when something... something hit us."

Alexei's hands trembled as he recalled the screams of his crew, the shrieking alarms, and the sickening crunch as metal tore apart like tin foil. The ship had buckled and groaned like a dying whale before settling into an eerie, motionless silence broken only by the soft hiss of oxygen escaping through a gaping rent in the hull.

"We lost communications, navigation, and life support almost immediately. My crew patched the holes, rerouted power, kept me alive. They..." Alexei paused, choking down the lump forming in his throat. "They sacrificed themselves so that I might have this final chance."

He looked up at the viewscreen, a starscape smeared and distorted as though viewed through tears. The Milky Way arced overhead like a swath of spilled paint, stretching out forever in both directions. Earth, home, was somewhere in there, reduced to nothing more than a distant point of light, unreachable even at relativistic speeds.

"I don't know how long I have left, Earth. Ship's core is failing, oxygen scrubbers are offline. I'm alone in the blackness, waiting for the end. I wish I could see stars again, feel the sun on my face one last time. I wish... I wish I hadn't left my daughter alone."

Alexei's voice cracked. He buried his face in his gloved hands, shoulders shaking silently. In the blackness behind his eyelids, he saw his little girl, her eyes wide and innocent, filled with love and trust. Trust that he would come home to her, like he always promised. Like father like daughter, except she'd had no inkling of the darkness waiting in the stars.

"I'm sorry, malyshka. Papa tried. Papa really did. I hope you know that." He sniffled and wiped away tears, sniffling against the cold recycled air.

He looked down at the logbook resting on the console beside him, opened to a page of his own unsteady handwriting. He'd done his best to chronicle everything - the readings, the crew's final moments, everything he could remember. It wasn't much, but it was all that remained of them now.

A shrill warning klaxon pierced the air, startling him upright. Alexei winced, clapping hands over his ears. He knew that sound all too well now. It meant one thing and one thing alone.

"Hull breach detected in engineering," a cool synthetic voice intoned. "initiating emergency seal protocol. Core temperature critical. Imminent meltdown in T-minus 60 seconds."

"Shit, come on!" Alexei growled, frantically typing commands into the unresponsive keyboard. The damage reports scrolled past too quickly to register. They were seconds away from total systems failure. He'd be dead in minutes.

"Fuck me, why does everything have to go wrong at once today?" He slammed a fist against the console, swearing viciously under his breath. The pain barely registered compared to the hollow ache inside him.

"T-minus 45 seconds until core meltdown. Please evacuate the ship immediately."

"Yeah, thanks, no shit," Alexei snarled, flipping through the useless diagnostic reports for anything, anything at all that might still respond. "Come on, come on..."

There. The emergency distress beacon. It was an outside chance at best, but it was the last hope they had. He hit the override and began praying to any god or devil that might still give a shit.

A sudden jolt rocked the bridge, throwing him against the restraints. Warning Klaxons screamed shrill warnings as red emergency lights strobed frantically. The Orpheus bucked and writhed like a dying thing thrashing in its death throes, structural integrity alarms shrieking a final, agonized cry of protest.

"Core breach in progress. Impending structural failure."

"Blyat'! Hold together, hold together just a little longer!" Alexei roared, straining against the harness, knuckles white as he hammered uselessly at unresponsive controls. The ship groaned and creaked like an old wooden hull straining against a stormy sea.

"T-minus 30 seconds until core breach. Please evacuate the ship immediately."

"No," Alexei ground out through teeth clenched together so hard they threatened to crack. "No, no, no, no..."

The Orpheus shuddered as though mortally wounded, plates buckling and groaning like a great metal thing dying on the battlefield. Warning klaxons reached a shrieking crescendo before suddenly cutting off into a deafening, numbing silence.

"Core breach neutralized. Containment successful."

Alexei sagged back against the seat, panting raggedly as relief washed through him like a cool wave. "Son of a bitch," he wheezed. He'd done it. Somehow, impossibly, he'd done it. They'd done it. "Thank you, crew."

A distant part of him registered the soft hiss of escaping atmosphere, the unmistakable sound of vacuum greedily devouring oxygen. The emergency bulkheads hadn't sealed completely. It didn't matter anymore. He'd bought himself maybe minutes at best.

The sky scraper swayed, as she watched the window in front of her on the 21st floor explode. Glass shattered like a thousand tiny razor blades, biting into her skin as she screamed and instinctively covered her face with her arms. Wind howled through the sudden gaping hole, whipping her hair and clothing in a frenzy. Her heart hammered against her ribs as a cold sweat prickled across her body.

"Oh God, oh God, oh God," she chanted, backing away from the ledge. Her high heels skittered across the polished marble, threatening to slip out from under her. The glass littered floor made the task nearly impossible.

"Get control," she growled at herself, steadying herself against the nearest cubicle. The office was eerily quiet save for the wind's earsplitting shrill and the distant sirens wailing from far below. She gulped down a deep breath, willing herself to look past the dizzying drop-off.

The scene below defied reason. Fires raged like hellish bonfires, devouring everything in sight. Skyscrapers lay crumbled in heaps, as though some angry giant child had tossed them aside like discarded Legos. Ambulances and fire trucks swarmed like insignificant ants, useless against the apocalyptic destruction.

A sickening groan reverberated through the building's foundation. Sheer terror gripped her, paralyzing her limbs. The structure listed to the side, metal screeching like nails across a chalkboard. Then, as though time slowed to a crawl, she watched in frozen horror as the entire glass exterior peeled away like a ripe banana skin, revealing the guts of the skyscraper's skeleton.

"No, please, please God no," she sobbed, hands clasped together in supplication. But prayers were useless here. The ground fell away like a giant trapdoor, pulling her screaming into the abyss. The wind rushing past stole the screams from her throat as gravity took hold. The city streets rushed up to greet her at an alarming rate, growing larger with each passing second until they became a smudge of concrete and glass.

The impact never came. Instead, she slammed into something solid yet yielding, like a giant trampoline. Air exploded from her lungs as she ricocheted off the unseen force, plummeting again before slamming against something else. Again and again she rebounded, the world spinning dizzyingly until up became down and left became right.

She landed hard against unforgiving concrete, stars dancing on the edge of her vision. Groaning, she pushed herself up on shaking arms, spitting out a mouthful of blood. Slowly, the world came into focus. She lay sprawled across the remains of a toppled hot dog cart, its previous occupant splattered against the wall like an abstract painting.

Bile rose in her throat as she pushed herself upright, retching until there was nothing left except bile and horror. Trembling violently, she glanced around wildly. The scene defied description - it looked like someone had taken a giant industrial-strength blender to Times Square during rush hour. Twisted metal, concrete slabs, bodies parts and rubble stretched as far as she could see. The stench of death and gasoline choked her senses.

A low moan drifted across the rubble-strewn landscape, barely audible over the crackling flames and distant screams. She whirled toward the sound, her shredded and bloodied cocktail dress fluttering in the wind. A hand reached skyward from under a slab of jagged concrete, fingers twitching weakly. In a daze, she stumbled toward it, hardly registering the glass slicing into the soles of her bare feet.

"Help me," croaked a hoarse voice, male and weak. "Please, help me."

"Hold on, hold on," she wheezed, straining against the weight of the massive chunk. It budged an inch, then another. Sweat mingled with grime and tears streamed down her filthy face. Finally, with a herculean growl, she heaved the slab aside, revealing a haggard, unconscious face.

"Oh God, please don't let him be dead," she gasped, falling to her knees beside him. Pulse fluttered faintly in his neck. She tore shreds off her tattered dress, wadding them against gaping wounds across his chest and leg. Crimson soaked into the white material instantly.

"Wake up, wake up damn you," she sobbed, shaking him violently. His eyes fluttered open a crack, unfocused and glassy. "Stay with me! I've got you, okay? My name's... my God, I don't even remember my Goddamn name but just hang on, okay?"

"Amelia," he croaked, voice barely a whisper. "My wife, she's still up there. Please, please find her."

She clutched his cold hands, nodding frantically even though she knew there could be no survivors higher than this hellish level. Sirens wailed faintly in the distance. "I promise. I swear on everything holy, I won't stop until I find her." Even if it kills me too. "Just hang on just hang on just hang on..."

The world spun sickeningly as she felt herself slipping away, exhaustion and shock finally catching up. She crumpled atop him, bloodied hands still clasped tight in hers. His ragged breathing slowed until it faded away to nothing. Sirens grew fainter until they vanished altogether, leaving only the crackling flames and mournful wind as a dirge for the dead.

As darkness claimed her, she wondered blearily why everything looked wrong - why was the sky black instead of blue, why did the sun cast an eerie crimson glow instead of reassuring yellow light. Why did the air taste like metal and ash instead of smog and exhaust. Why did the world end today instead of the end of time. The last thought fluttered away like a moth to the flames as she succumbed to merciful oblivion, the last spark of life guttering out like a snuffed candlewick in the gathering gloom. And in the far reaches of space, a once vibrant blue marble slowly winked out, extinguished like a failed star against the infinite dark.

THE END

We'll keep fighting until our last breath drawn. Til' no resistance left to be broke. Til' they're nothing left standing between us and that sweet taste victory we've all been waiting so goddamned long to savor on bitter tongues.

The rain pelts against the windowpanes like hailstones as I huddle deeper into the shadows of the empty apartment. My breath condenses in foggy puffs despite the suffocating humidity. I shift the grip of my plasma blaster, fingers sweat slick on the smooth trigger guard. Waiting. Watching.

The door handle twists. Lock clicks. Clicks again.

I tense. Hold my breath.

The door swings inward, creaking on rusty hinges. Black silhouettes spill into the room, weapons drawn. My eyes narrow to slits. I count the shapes. One. Two. Three.

"Clear," a gruff voice growls.

I exhale slowly. Too early. Too soon.

The third figure steps into the light and my heart lurches into a gallop. recognition slams into me like a freight train. My foster-brother-turned-traitor, Rorik. He looks different. Harder. Older than his twenty-two years. A jagged scar slashes across his formerly smooth brow. His eyes glitter like obsidian flakes in the gloom.

Betrayer.

Anger flares in my gut, scorching away any shred of childhood sentimentality. I finger the trigger. I want to see that smug smirk burn off his face with a well-placed bolt from this baby. Make him scream like the Judas he is. But not yet.

Rorik strides to the window, pulls aside the heavy drapes, and peers into the downpour. "She's here," he snarls, voice barely above a rumble. "I can feel it."

"Bullshit," I whisper into my radio cuff, barely containing a sneer. "Your instincts are about as sharp as a butter knife, asshole."

He tenses, head snapping left and right like a cornered ferret. I duck lower. Hold my breath.

"Shut up, you two. Listen," the larger silhouette barks.

Rorik curses under his breath and holsters his sidearm. "You heard the man. Fucking listen."

Silence except for rain and distant sirens.

"What is it—" the third man begins.

BANG. BANG. BANG.

Glass explodes. Plaster and wood spray in a blinding haze. I don't think. Just react. I roll, pop up firing as I rise, sweeping left to right, muzzle flashes lighting up the room like strobe-lit hell.

"Fuck, what—"

"NooOOOhhhh!"

The meaty thud of heavy bodies falling onto floorboards. Sputtering moans cut short with sharp, wet cracks.

Then only rain pattering against shattered panes and the coppery tang of spent powder hangs heavy in the air.

I sling the plasma blaster over my shoulder and stalk into the ruins of what was supposed to be our meeting point. Stepping gingerly to avoid the spreading pools of crimson and oozing lumps, I stop beside what remains of Foster-traitor. His dead eyes stare accusingly at me. Too late, you sonofabitch.

Heavy footfalls pound down the hall, accompanied by huffing curses. "Get in here, you useless—"

I spin, plasma humming as I bring the barrel up nose-level with the panting, sweat-drenched enforcer's surprise.

"Down," I snarl, "or join your dead little friends."

His hands fly up in a white-flag surrender gesture. "Don't shoot, don't shoot!" His eyes plead silently for mercy.

"Too late for that shit, pal." I depress the trigger.

White light blossoms like an angry daffodil. He vanishes in a blossom of smoke and steam.

I whirl, already moving toward the open door. "Shit," I snarl under my breath, chest tight like a vice. "Shit, shit, fuck."

Science Fiction: The Last Transmission - Write a story that takes place entirely within a spaceship's cockpit as the sole surviving crew member attempts to send a final message back to Earth before the ship's power runs out. The story should explore themes of isolation, sacrifice, and the importance of human connection in the face of adversity. 800-1000 words.

Captain Aria was strapped into the pilot's chair, hands trembling as she tried desperately to manually keep the ship's systems alive for just one more precious second. The console was an eerie blue, only the essential life signs still blinking. Emergency lighting casted a sickly pallor over her exhausted form.

"Come on, come on..." she wheezed, willing the old bird to cling onto life for just long enough to get this done.

It'd been hours since the dreadful impact with the rogue asteroid flock that'd left them adrift, tumbling aimlessly in the black abyss of space. The rest of crew was gone, scattered like stars across the void. Just her and this tin can hurtling into final silence.

Her gloved fingers jabbed at the dying communications panel. "Aria. Aria. Come in." Static crackled back.

Static. The final message received at Earth, if they'd received anything at all. If they still knew she still breathed in here, alone.

Her eyes blurred with tears as she recalled the faces of her crew - their banter, their lives cut short like starburst. She'd seen enough wars end in space to fill three lifetimes. This though, watching your shipmates snuffed like blown-out birthday candles, that'll never leave the mind.

"C'mon baby, let me say goodbye." Captain's voice a broken whisper.

The console sparked as its life breathed out in a wheeze of breath. "Affirmative," a synthetic voice croaked. "Transmission channel active for remaining 2m 15 seconds. Commence final log."

Aria drew a long breath, steadying herself for one last push. She'd been saving it up all along, just in case this moment ever came. A lifetime of love, laughter, loss. All down to one final line. Her fingers shook.

"I love you," she finally said into the void, voice breaking. "Tell them... tell them it was worth it all. Tell them..."

Her eyes welled up as she remembered him, as if he stood there now beside her in that chair. "Tell them it was worth it for you."

Static answered back. The cockpit grew deathly quiet save for the ticking countdown clock.

"C'mon, baby..." she implored, willing just one more word out of nowhere. Just one thing left unsaid. One final breath of life from a soul so nearly spent.

Silence.

Then, a ping. A distant echo of something living, something warm in all that cold.

She startled, craning round to spot it.

There it lay, nestled behind the pilot's seat like a lost child. Her mother's old keepsake. Still operational. Still clinging onto life like it knew somehow to wait for this very second.

Aria lunged for it, fumbling with shaking hands to draw it forth. Clicked the power on. Watched it flare to life.

One final line. One final word. Her final will and testament to Earth.

"Goodbye, everyone," she said hoarse. "Goodbye."

"Message received," the AI voice crackled out, one last time before the light went forever. "Goodbye Aria."

And then, only static, as the stars died and the universe fell still in space and in silence eternal.

THE END.

Brainstorm 40x

The BRAINSTORM process was developed by David_AU.

Some of the core principals behind this process are discussed in this scientific paper : Progressive LLaMA with Block Expansion .

However I went in a completely different direction from what was outlined in this paper.

What is "Brainstorm" ?

The reasoning center of an LLM is taken apart, reassembled, and expanded.

In this case for this model: 40 times

Then these centers are individually calibrated. These "centers" also interact with each other. This introduces subtle changes into the reasoning process. The calibrations further adjust - dial up or down - these "changes" further. The number of centers (5x,10x etc) allow more "tuning points" to further customize how the model reasons so to speak.

The core aim of this process is to increase the model's detail, concept and connection to the "world", general concept connections, prose quality and prose length without affecting instruction following.

This will also enhance any creative use case(s) of any kind, including "brainstorming", creative art form(s) and like case uses.

Here are some of the enhancements this process brings to the model's performance:

  • Prose generation seems more focused on the moment to moment.
  • Sometimes there will be "preamble" and/or foreshadowing present.
  • Fewer or no "cliches"
  • Better overall prose and/or more complex / nuanced prose.
  • A greater sense of nuance on all levels.
  • Coherence is stronger.
  • Description is more detailed, and connected closer to the content.
  • Simile and Metaphors are stronger and better connected to the prose, story, and character.
  • Sense of "there" / in the moment is enhanced.
  • Details are more vivid, and there are more of them.
  • Prose generation length can be long to extreme.
  • Emotional engagement is stronger.
  • The model will take FEWER liberties vs a normal model: It will follow directives more closely but will "guess" less.
  • The MORE instructions and/or details you provide the more strongly the model will respond.
  • Depending on the model "voice" may be more "human" vs original model's "voice".

Other "lab" observations:

  • This process does not, in my opinion, make the model 5x or 10x "smarter" - if only that was true!
  • However, a change in "IQ" was not an issue / a priority, and was not tested or calibrated for so to speak.
  • From lab testing it seems to ponder, and consider more carefully roughly speaking.
  • You could say this process sharpens the model's focus on it's task(s) at a deeper level.

The process to modify the model occurs at the root level - source files level. The model can quanted as a GGUF, EXL2, AWQ etc etc.

Directory Structure 

large-v3-turbo/
├── whisper-large-v3-turbo-q*.gguf       # Candle-compatible GGUF models (root)

├── tokenizer.json             # Tokenizer for Candle
└── whisper.cpp/               # whisper.cpp-compatible models
    └── whisper-large-v3-turbo-q*.gguf

Format Compatibility

  • Root directory (whisper-large-v3-turbo-*.gguf): Use with Candle (Rust ML framework)

    • Tensor names include model. prefix (e.g., model.encoder.conv1.weight)
    • Requires config-large-v3-turbo.json and tokenizer-large-v3-turbo.json

  • whisper.cpp/ directory: Use with whisper.cpp (C++ implementation)

    • Tensor names without model. prefix (e.g., encoder.conv1.weight)
    • Compatible with whisper.cpp CLI tools
    • Both directories contain .gguf files, not .bin files
